text: A whaler swears he counted an island off the southern lanes that was there on the way out and gone on the way home. The Chartwrights have filed it anyway.
The Gate-Tithe is cheating us in both directions. It keeps the gold in Ironfort and sends the paper to Goldwind.
The Widow's Teeth are singing a new tune. The old women say a boat will be lost in the Gap before the Murk is over.
Johann Faust has been seen in a Greyhaven tavern with a man who wears the Last Psalm's badge. Nobody knows which side he means to take.
Mortimer Vanris will sell the Stormguard to the Heartland before the year is out. His brother has already written to the Council about it.
Tana Sukuun has sold a Dreadmaw to the Heartland. The buyer is a Vol Kaern agent, and the saurian is named after the Vol Kaern tower.
Dio Emberheart has been seen walking in the Sunhold gardens. The people who saw him say he was not quite the same man who walked there last year.
Kastan Vol Kaern is buying Bastion's debts through the Zane house. He will own the Frontier's gate before the Council knows he has begun.
Sissix-the-Comet has lost a heat for the first time in two seasons. The jockey who beat her has a Vossreth brand on his wrist and no memory of the race.
A Scarlet Mother's priest was seen in Southhaven buying the Fennick factors' coffee in bulk. Nobody says what he wants with so much of it.
The Vorthani First Ascent has taken in a guest who will not carry a stone. The monks say she is not a guest.
The Frost Elves have stopped raiding the Auroral Vault. The Frost Elves say Vukharr is dreaming of something new.
Mira has been seen at Crystalhaven with Granny Skerrow's grandson. A smuggler's heir is never seen with a wrecker's grandson unless one of them means to take the other's chair.
The black circle in the sky is spreading. A whale-fleet that sailed too far last year came back with the sky over its masts gone black.
Emri has been seen swimming past the Drowned Colonnade with a bundle of silver on her back. Nobody has asked her what she is carrying.
heardAt: heard in the Sea and the Coral Kingdoms

text: The Red Choir has started singing on a quiet night, when there is no blood in the water. The Tidecallers say the song is coming up the Starfall Reef.
heardAt: heard in the Sea and the Coral Kingdoms

text: Pelagar has been buying the Starfall coral in bulk. The Glass Gardens have stopped trading with Pelagar in return.
heardAt: heard in the Sea and the Coral Kingdoms

text: The Old Shells answered a question last month that no one had asked. The answer was the name of a ship, and the ship has not been seen since.
heardAt: heard in the Sea and the Coral Kingdoms

text: The spark ferrets at Ironfort customs won't go near one particular noble's luggage. They don't spark. They hide.
The dry road. The roads Below run island to island, and a smuggler who knew them could walk a cargo from Black Harbor to Goldwind without paying a single harbor due.
Sailors' songs count the great dragons of the world as nine. A Highspire star-reader once counted ten, and the University took her charts away.
Highspire's astronomers keep one star on their charts that crosses the sky the wrong way.
A deep hum comes up through the floor of the Darlath mines at night, and the Cindren who work near it go dim.
One crate of Darlath stone in twelve leaves Everfall marked 'broken' and is never seen at the refinery.
The Cindren of Everfall say the Glass Forest chimed thirteen times last Graveday, and it has only ever chimed in twelves.
The dark elf at the Rusty Blade paid for his rooms with a coin nobody could name. Old Daun has nailed it over the bar.
Pale moons. New Tides ring dull, say the scale-men of Fairweather, and they have started weighing them. The Mint says nothing.
The Gilded Shallows are glowing at night now, even when the tide is low. The Concord says it is a blessing. The Registry says it is a fire.
The Singing Cliffs sounded a chord last spring that no harbor-master had ever heard. The weather that followed was perfectly ordinary, which worried them more.
The Cathedral Green's trees have started to grow new graves. The Liriath say it is their own dead, but no one of their kind has died in the Green in forty years.
A Galven crew sailed into a storm off Stormreach and came back with every mark on their arms burning white, laughing.
A Florian in the Cathedral Green has seen four dawns, and the Liriath have stopped speaking above a whisper near her.
A Tarvan on the Giant's Table heard the Sleeping Giant turn over in its sleep. She went home and sold every horse she had.
The Tobbin pride say Saffrane's famous Black Rose was theirs first, and that they still have the bill of sale.
A Sporrn healer came up to Southhaven with medicine nobody asked for, three days before the fever arrived.
A court envoy came ashore at Easthold with bells on both wrists and asked to speak to whoever keeps the harbor's oldest promise.
A lampet in Greyhaven brought up a gold ring nobody aboard had lost, and the harbor-master's wife has been very quiet since.
The lighthouse keeper at Saltreach swears her mouse put its tail out the night a ship went by with no lights at all.
A courier's rainfrog sat on a Council dispatch through a whole shipwreck. The dispatch was dry. The courier was not so lucky.
Somewhere below the coral there is a reef made entirely of buttons, and every button badger in the islands knows the way.
A button badger in Silverport keeps bringing home silver buttons with a house crest nobody can place.
heardAt: heard in a Silverport tailor's shop

text: They say a teacup moth will not warm a cup that has been poisoned. Nobody has been brave enough to test it twice.
A great auroc broke its tether at Bastion and walked straight to the Tarvan moors, as if it knew the way.
A Goldwind noble offered a fortune for a street child's mirror plover. The child said no, and the plover said something worse.
A hush owl went quiet at a wedding in Saltreach last Storm Water, and the groom has not been seen since.
Captain Blackstorm: he once outmaneuvered the whole Armada during a King Tide.
heardAt: the docks, about the Most Wanted

text: The new Tides are lighter than the old ones. The Mint says it is the wear of the dies.
A Harbinger made Ironfort to Goldwind in eleven days. The Admiralty will not say how.
A grandmother in Sunhold has a waybook whose blank last page has started filling itself in.
The Midnight Patron has been buying every old chart of the far south, and paying in uncut Krysta.
A memory-pearl sold in Pearl Groove shows a woman's face on the Sunken Thrones. She is looking up, and she is smiling.
heardAt: heard in the Sea and the Coral Kingdoms

text: Masons in seven dwarven holds have stopped talking about what they found on the shelf beside the wall.
The dwarves have an old word for the drow, and they will not say it in front of a banker.
Progeny of three different Lords were seen hunting side by side in the Southern Wilds, all chasing the same pale animal.
The empty chair in the Admiralty's High Command was dusted last week. Nobody admits to ordering it.
The Platinum Ten walk among us. Nobody knows who they are.
The first of the Ten has held the top of the Ranking since before anyone's grandmother was born. The Chroniclers stopped writing down her age.
heardAt: a Lodge Chronicler, after his third kellum

text: A giant of a Frost Elf walks the ice with a hooded priest who never eats. The Hunters posted a contract on him, and Albion Tempest took it.
Siroc the Swift: he has escaped the Armada more than a dozen times.
heardAt: the docks, about the Most Wanted

text: A Pursuer came to Southhaven hunting an oath-breaker, and the man she took away was a whaler who could not stop humming.
The Chartwrights keep the tortoise islands off the public charts. Ask a surveyor where they are and watch his tortoise look at him.
Two of the Twelve Flags have stopped speaking to each other on the Spire Floor, and every factor in Goldwind is buying rope.
The Registrar exists. He is a tall man in grey who visits the University's cellars at night, and the University denies he has ever come to the city.
The Sunhold terraces grow a brightleaf that the Registry buys every leaf of, and nobody has ever been allowed to taste it.
A hearth newt in Kaldmark slept on the same coal for a whole winter, and the hold that kept it lost no one to the cold.
A cricket sang a whole crew to sleep the night their ship was boarded. The thieves took the cargo and left the cricket.
A pair of promise doves were seen flying out to sea, both of them, together. Nobody wants to think about what that means.
A promise dove flew in circles over Goldwind for three days. Its mate's keeper had sailed into the fog off the Frontier, and the dove could not decide where she was.
There's a mirror plover in Goldwind that talks like a man nobody in the city remembers.
A mirror plover in Easthold still talks like a captain who drowned eleven years ago. His widow brings it bread every morning.
A pirate in irons at Ironfort walked free because his knot crab picked the rope on the gallows.
No leak rat will board the new Vindicator at Stormreach. The yard says it is the smell of fresh pitch. The crew says it isn't.
A gutter parrot in Hollowkey knows a Council admiral's private name for his wife, and says it every evening at the sixth bell.
A Greyhaven cormorant came back from the fog with a fish no one in the north had ever seen.
A noble's taster bat refused a cup at a Heartland wedding, and the groom's family left before dessert.
heardAt: heard in the salons of Goldwind

text: A counting jackdaw at the Reckoners' Hall will not sit on one clerk's desk. The clerk has asked to be moved.
An ink octopus copied a stranger's face onto a ledger page. The stranger has been looking for that page ever since.
A sail-loft in Goldwind has a darning spider that only mends sails for ships that come home.
Glider squirrels are carrying love notes across Goldwind's roofs for a noble daughter and a dock clerk. Half the city knows; her father does not.
Silverport's gaming houses have started checking guests' pockets for geckos at the door.
A bookmark silverfish in the University's library stopped on a page that is not in the book.
A sailor's snail has been pointing out to sea for a month, toward no island on any chart.
Every drum hare on the Northreach moors drummed at once one night last winter, and nobody found anything at all.
An echo finch in Bastion repeats a phrase in a voice nobody in the house recognizes.
A dreamcurl hedgehog left its sleeper's chest in the middle of the night and would not go back. The sleeper has not been the same.
heardAt: heard in a Frontier hedgerow village

text: A spark ferret at Ironfort's customs house went mad over a crate of 'pottery' bound north.
The thumb raptors of one Jakupur street have started hunting something too small for anyone else to see.
A veil butterfly went clear as glass in the middle of a Goldwind ball, and stayed that way all night.
heardAt: heard in the salons of Goldwind

text: A moss sloth's moss kept a Hunter alive for three days in the deep green, and the sloth would not leave until the healers came.
A trail mongoose followed a stolen saddle across half the Wilds and led its person straight to a Southhaven magistrate's stable.
A Frost Elf left a scarf stoat at a stranger's door in the Long Night, and the stranger lived.
Every hush owl in a Snowvah graveyard puffed up at once on the last King Tide.
A landfall petrel led a lost whaler to an island that was not there when the Chartwrights went to look.
A pearl diver's seahorse blew its bubble for a drowning stranger, and the Glass Gardens sent the diver a pearl the next morning.
Every tide anemone in Southhaven closed at noon on the same day last year, out of turn, for exactly as long as it takes to say a prayer.
An anemone on an Easthold windowsill knew the tide had turned at home, while its keeper was a month's sail away.
A lodge hound at the Jakupur Lodge has started tracking something the Board has not posted a contract for.
A caravan's roof goats spotted bandits on the Frontier road a full hour before the drivers did, and the bandits are still wondering how.
A tidehound at Greyhaven pulled a stranger out of the sea who will not say what ship he came from.
A tern carried a doctor-wanted note to Ironfort's tower from a ship that never came into harbor.
The pod that guides ships through the Widow's Teeth has stopped answering one pilot's whistle.
The customs house at Varan Port has started dragging the water under the piers. They have not found an eel yet.
The Stillwrights' wrack cows refused to graze one honeywrack bed all summer, and that bed's kellum tasted wrong.
A ferry turtle in the Heartland channels was late for the first time in sixty years. Nobody knows where it went for that hour.
The Reckoners' vault geese were silent the night a ledger went missing.
The swineherds swear the gutter pigs will not go down one alley in Goldwind's lower streets.
An Aurelion smith says her bellows toad will not blow for blades meant for the Imperium.
The dawn duck parade at Sunhold went the wrong way round the terraces one morning, and that season's leaf was the best in twenty years.
A Silverport silk farm is raising a moth whose silk shines in the dark. The other farms want to know how.
A moorhorn herd walked off the Northreach moors in a single night, ribbons and all, and was found standing in a circle of stones.
A fishing family's kin-knit pattern turned up on a drowned man nobody in the village knew.
The glint moles of one Frontier mine are digging down, not toward any vein, and the miners have stopped following.
The herd otters of the Nine Mouths have started driving the fish away from one river village. The village has done something.
heardAt: heard on the rivers of the Nine Mouths

text: A rimehound team stopped dead on the ice and would not go on. The sledge went around. The crevasse they smelled is still being measured.
The whale-wolves did not come for the tongue after the last kill. Frosthold has not decided whether to worry.
A strider crab walked out of the sea at a market harbor with no rider and a basket full of bells.
A tidesteed with an empty shell saddle has been seen off Easthold three nights running.
One lamp-shoal in Thalassar has started swimming a new round, and the courts are arguing about where it leads.
Someone is selling reefpurple dye in Silverport at half the price. The Coral peoples want to know where it comes from.
A haulbeetle in a dwarven tunnel stopped and would not move, and the miners found a door behind the rock it stopped at.
An old chartback in Goldwind has a shell whose plates match an island no chart shows. Three surveyors have asked to buy its charts. It is not for sale.
A Pocchin family turned down a whole island for their oldest grommoth. Twice.
A dragonborn veteran in Bastion still wears his imperial insignia, and the garrison has decided to let him.
The Cistern Door. At the bottom of Goldwind's oldest cistern is a dwarven wall, and someone has been working its mortar from the other side.
Drow eyes. A drow's eyes shine in the dark, and the older the drow, the dimmer they shine.
Hrothgar Icevein: he hunts the Frost Elves who exiled him.
heardAt: the docks, about the Most Wanted

text: A gnome workshop in Goldwind has built a clock that runs backward during the Still Days.
A goblin at the Knot is wearing a Council admiral's hat and has a very good story about it.
A goliath came down from the high ranges with a bead nobody has the right to wear: one for climbing the Sky Anvil.
A half-elf interpreter in Silverport has been offered a fortune to mistranslate a single word at a treaty table.
A halfling inn on the Heartland river roads has never once run out of beds, however many guests arrive.
A Jakupur trader and a Frontier lord were seen drinking together in Goldwind, laughing. Both deny it.
A kobold warren under Duskmire has started selling maps of the tunnels below. Every map is a little different.
A lizardfolk elder repainted herself in a pattern no one has worn in a hundred years.
An orc chieftain in the south is said to have buried a daemon-mask at sea, on purpose, with a Telling sung over it.
Someone drew steel at the Soldiers' Rest last winter. The springs ran cold for a week.
A swimmer reached the bottom of Malim's Stair laughing, without a scratch, and swore the river had carried her the whole way.
A guide says one of the bones on the white flats has moved, a little, every year since he was a boy.
On the last night of the King Tide, a third moon was seen in the Mirrormere.
Something pale has been walking the bottom of the Whalefall Gardens at low water, tending them.
The Stillwater has moved three leagues west. The Armada's charts say it has always been there. The sailors say it has always been moving.
heardAt: heard in the Sea and the Coral Kingdoms

text: The Old Shells have surfaced at the Stillwater three times this year. They used to come up once in a generation.
In one Frontier village the fire was lit every morning for a year after the last keeper died, and nobody ever saw who lit it.
A Returning Cup in Easthold turned itself upright in the window, and the sailor it waited for walked in the next morning.
A Goldwind stillhouse has a cask of Icebrand old enough to have come off the first whaling ships. It is not for sale, which is why everyone wants it.
A wild swordtooth pack has learned to wait outside Jakupur's gates at the hour the caravans leave.
A Jakupur noble walled his garden with live thornbacks instead of stone. His neighbors sleep badly.
A lashtail in the Maw-Pit broke three shields in one bout and then refused to fight anyone without one.
A glidetalon carried a scout's message forty miles over the jungle in a single afternoon, and the scout has never been found.
A Skyfin rider claims she flew high enough to see the whole south at once, and that something was looking back.
The oldest loamback in Jakupur's quarries will only haul stone for one family, and that family is three generations dead.
An altisaur carried a wedding party across a flooded river without spilling a single cup.
A craghorn gored a tax collector in a southern village and the magistrate ruled it self-defense.
A murkstrider walked a lost child home through the bog and would not leave until it was fed.
A trader camped for a week on an island in the delta. On the eighth morning the island left.
The razorfins of one river have stopped taking the bait, and the boatmen say they are waiting for something bigger.
A bellowback herd lay down all at once on the savanna and would not rise until the earthquake had passed.
Every cluckmaw in a Jakupur village laid an egg with a red speckle on the same morning.
A Jakupur scribe swears his quillhen's quills only write the truth.
The White Flame's bounty on wild gloamhides was paid twice last year, both times for the same animal.
Nobody has ever painted the Imperium's Grand Inquisitor. The Frontier spies who claim to have seen him won't say what he looked like.
Sailors back from Khard Muur say Valengrad crowned King Rune last year. They crowned him the year before too, and he was buried in between.
heardAt: a sailor back from the west

text: The Wrong Coast. The quarantined waters of the far south are "plague waters," the Council says. Southern sailors tell stories of grey ships with no names that sail without lanterns, and of the Hum: a note under hearing that you feel in the hull on calm nights. Never hum along.
Goldspire's heir was seen at a pawnbroker's on the Duskmire road, in a borrowed cloak.
Goldwind's lamps burn cleaner since Frosthold changed its oil. The lamplighters say the smoke smells faintly of coins.
Reinhardt Holst buys a drink for every old pirate in Hollowkey and asks each of them the same question: whose colors sank the Sea Seraph?
Damyel's ship made Mumit from Southhaven in five days, against the wind. The fastest Justicar in the Emerald Wrath needs two weeks.
Stormwater from the Stormreach spring tastes of the sea where it used to taste of rock.
Fishers off Stormreach netted a brass hatch the size of a door, with a wheel on it.
Don't sail west. Out past the edge of the charts lies cursed Xathnatraz, the isle where the dark of the old Eon was sealed. Ships that go looking for it come back with fewer people, or not at all.
The Maw-Pit is holding a fight this month that does not have a condemned man in it. It has a child.
Abyssara: what falls into the southwestern trench does not come back; what comes back is changed.
Someone is buying every reefpurple dye that comes through Pearl Groove. The Council cannot find the buyer, and the Pelagar house will not say.
The center socket. The Spire Floor has a thirteenth flag-socket at its center that has never held a flag, and the Charterhouse Company wants it very badly.
Theodora Nightshade: she has slipped in and out of the Reckoners' Hall.
heardAt: the docks, about the Most Wanted

text: The Rose House signs every contract twice: once in ink, and once in something that does not dry.
Lady Xanthea Alastor and Lady Lysandria Caelvaron dance together at every Veldane wedding, and at no other.
Halsof Varselis has been asked to take the Five's chair, and he has said no three times. The fourth time he may say yes.
The Long Night will be early this year. The Brine Brotherhood's oil-houses are already sold for the next two winters.
Every year on the night of the Maw, someone leaves a red-bladed knife on the reef where Blackheart fell.
Children in Goldwind say the Council Hall's copper weathervane turns to face Lactinius Windcaller wherever he walks.
Nobody has ever seen the Iron Swan take on coal.
"Painted" Cora: she leaves a painted red rose on every ship she plunders.

text: A blackened copper Bit on a dead man's tongue means one thing in the Undertow: don't ask.
The Undertow: the smuggler's web that moves what the harbors won't. Everyone has a cousin who knows someone.
A few of Johann Faust’s relatives suspect he may have a son born out of wedlock. None of them can agree on who the mother might have been.

“Hyacinth Alastor and Reinhardt Holst were seen together at Lord Vanris’s Midsummer Gala. A chance conversation, they say. Of course. The drawing rooms are already wondering whether there is something more between the Rose House’s heir and the disinherited Holst.” (whispered behind a silk fan)
heardAt: whispered in noble drawing rooms after Lord Vanris’s Midsummer Gala

text: “His lordship says the second pool is for a different color. The man who delivered the fish asked where the guests would place their wagers.” (a Heartland household servant)

text: He has a year’s salary now and still comes in just to ask what she thinks of his hat.
heardAt: a customer at Vellune, on Radan Sunmere

text: For the first time in seventy years, the Stormchanters are talking about joining the other orc tribes in a war.
A thunderbird egg rests at the very top of the Stormchanters’ shrine. They say the tribe is keeping watch over it.

Hands off the Karnivool swear that at the last King Tide they saw an island the old songs call Anukáli, with a whole people on it, and a leviathan that followed them north, calling like a whale, until it sank. The Lodge says the Karnivool’s hands drink.
Leoric Thorne came home last year in a Hunter ship’s hold and not on her quarterdeck. Ten years gone, and the Lodge will not say where it found him.
